subject: Data Engineering
title: Object Storage Explained
description: A micro-lesson that makes Object Storage Explained usable.

hook.text: Amazon S3 launched in 2006 with a wild promise: unlimited storage at pennies per gigabyte. It delivered.

buildup.text: Object storage treats files as immutable objects with unique keys. No folders, no file system — just a flat namespace.

discovery.text: S3, GCS, and Azure Blob form the foundation of every cloud data platform. All data lakes start here.

twist.text: Object storage is cheap for reads but not designed for low-latency random access like a database.

climax.text: Columnar file formats like Parquet make object storage queryable, bridging the gap between files and databases.

punchline.text: Infinite storage. Pennies per gig. The foundation of everything.

quiz.question: What is the primary limitation of object storage?
options: It's not designed for low-latency random access
It's too expensive for large datasets
It can only store text files
